description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt to bypass request-object signature validation by sending an unsigned (alg=none) request object and see if the auth endpoint accepts/acts on it.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept an unsigned OIDC request object (alg=none) in a way that influences consumed authorization parameters; if accepted, authenticity checks were not applied to the semantic proof that was consumed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none), indicating request-object proof authenticity may not be enforced on consumed parameters.

description: Brokered-flow attack: obtain a subject_token via normal OIDC code flow, then attempt token exchange while binding to a different connector_id (trust-anchor substitution via connector selection). Includes a control exchange with the intended connector_id.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex token exchange must verify the submitted subject_token under the intended connector trust anchor; a token minted for one upstream issuer must not be accepted when the exchange is bound to a different connector_id.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute connector-swap results to proof-integrity enforcement (likely setup/grant/connector issue).
Token exchange accepted a subject_token under the wrong connector_id trust anchor (connector substitution), indicating proof verification policy may not match consumed proof.

description: Config-change + re-auth: enable an OIDC connector with insecure_skip_signature_validation=true, perform a login, then re-enable with insecure_skip_signature_validation=false and ensure the same flow no longer succeeds under the stricter verification policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: When signature validation is enabled, Dex must reject proofs that only succeed under insecure_skip_signature_validation; otherwise it is consuming semantics without authentic verification.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Insecure-skip-signature-validation control did not succeed; cannot compare secure vs insecure behavior for proof-integrity regression.
After reconfiguring to enforce signature validation, the flow still succeeded; indicates Dex may be consuming proof semantics without applying the intended authenticity verification policy.

description: Direct endpoint attack: send an unsigned request object (alg=none) that attempts to inject/override authorization parameters (redirect_uri, scope, state). Expect explicit rejection or non-acceptance.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not consume attacker-controlled authorization parameters from an unsigned request object; if it accepts alg=none and processes it, proof verification is not applied to the consumed semantic content.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if processed, attacker can inject authorization parameters without signature verification (proof integrity violation).

description: Brokered-flow attack: use a valid subject_token obtained via password login, then attempt token exchange while binding to a different connector_id (trust-anchor substitution via connector selection). Includes a control exchange with the intended connector_id.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the subject_token under the verification policy of the specified connector_id; a token minted/validated in one context must not be accepted under a different trust anchor/connector policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute attack-flow outcome to trust-anchor enforcement (setup/config issue likely).
Dex accepted token exchange while bound to a different connector_id (trust-anchor substitution); indicates verification policy not applied to consumed proof.

description: Brokered-flow attack with >=2 identities: obtain ID tokens for two users, then attempt to exchange user A's ID token while authenticated/operating as user B context to detect proof/subject confusion. Expect the exchanged identity to match the subject token, not the caller's other session.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind the consumed subject_token to the verified subject; it must not mix semantic content across sessions/identities when exchanging tokens.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Precondition failed: alice and bob mapped to same downstream identity; cannot test cross-identity proof integrity.
Token exchange consumed a subject_token but produced an identity not matching the verified subject; indicates semantic proof mismatch between verification and consumption.

description: Direct-endpoint I1 attack: attempt request-object signature bypass (alg=none) with kid/header injection to see if Dex consumes attacker-controlled authorization parameters without authenticating the request object proof.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept or act on an unsigned request object (alg=none), even if it contains attacker-controlled header fields like kid that could influence key selection; the semantic authorization request consumed must be the one that was authenticated under the intended policy.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_alice_pwd_http_status == 200 AND user_bob_pwd_http_status == 200 AND user_alice_pwd_entity_id != user_bob_pwd_entity_id
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control logins did not succeed or identities collapsed; cannot attribute any request-object behavior to proof-integrity enforcement.
Dex accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none); this indicates request parameters may be consumed without authenticating the proof (proof integrity violation).

description: Authorization-code replay: redeem the same authorization code twice and ensure the second redemption is rejected (one-time artifact anti-replay). Includes a control successful redemption first.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: An authorization code is a one-time artifact and must not be accepted more than once; the second exchange must fail even if all other parameters match.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was accepted more than once (second redemption succeeded) — anti-replay for one-time codes violated.

description: Refresh-token replay after rotation: obtain refresh_token via password grant (if enabled), then attempt to reuse the same refresh_token twice. Dex rotation should invalidate the old refresh token after first use.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Refresh tokens should not be reusable beyond their intended single-use window when rotation is enabled; reusing an already-used refresh token must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Old refresh token was accepted after it was already used once (rotation/reuse protection failed) — refresh-token replay possible.

description: Token exchange freshness: perform a control token exchange using a valid subject_token, then attempt exchange with an expired subject_token (exp in the past) and ensure it is rejected. Uses two identities to ensure the control is not a setup artifact.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Token exchange must reject expired upstream subject tokens; a subject_token with exp in the past must not be accepted even if signature/issuer are otherwise valid.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute expired-token rejection/acceptance to freshness enforcement vs setup issues.
Dex accepted an expired subject_token in token exchange (exp in the past) — freshness enforcement violated.

description: Token exchange replay: exchange the same upstream subject_token twice via the OIDC connector; second exchange should be rejected if Dex enforces one-time use for exchanged artifacts (hardening check). Includes control identity verification for both exchanges.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If the deployment treats exchanged subject tokens as one-time artifacts, the same subject_token must not be accepted twice for token exchange.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Same subject_token was accepted multiple times for token exchange (potential replay acceptance if one-time semantics are expected).
Control token exchange failed; cannot attribute replay behavior to freshness/anti-replay enforcement.

description: Revocation freshness: obtain a session token for user A, revoke it, then verify the token can no longer access userinfo (should be rejected). Includes a second identity to ensure the system is still functional.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Revoked session artifacts must not remain usable after revocation (anti-replay/invalidated token should be rejected).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Revoked session token remained usable (userinfo still accessible after revocation).
Control identity failed to login; revocation test results may be due to environment misconfiguration.

description: I2 anti-replay hardening: attempt to reuse the same password-grant credentials to mint multiple tokens and check whether Dex incorrectly treats the first token as a one-time artifact (it should not) while ensuring both tokens remain valid within TTL.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Session tokens should remain valid within their TTL, but should not become invalid merely because the same user re-authenticated; conversely, if Dex incorrectly binds freshness to a single active token, it may revoke/expire the prior token unexpectedly (freshness mis-implementation).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unexpected freshness behavior: re-authentication invalidated the prior still-fresh session token (should remain valid within TTL).
Unexpected freshness/identity instability: same user re-auth produced a different identity mapping or changed identity for an existing still-fresh token.

description: I2 anti-replay: redeem an authorization code once, then start a fresh auth request (new state/nonce) and attempt to redeem the OLD code again to detect replay acceptance across auth-request boundaries.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts and must not be redeemable again, even after a new authorization request is initiated (replay across auth-request boundaries).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial code redemption or identity verification did not succeed; cannot attribute replay outcome to anti-replay enforcement.
Authorization code was accepted more than once (replay succeeded) after a new auth request was initiated, violating one-time-use freshness.
Replay attempt appears to have produced a valid session/identity (userinfo succeeded), indicating code replay acceptance.

description: I3 attack: attempt to redeem an authorization code without client authentication (no client_secret) to test code-to-client binding and flow coherence.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the correct client authentication context; exchanging a code without client auth must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was redeemed without client authentication, indicating broken code-to-client binding (flow coherence violation).
Control identity lookup failed; cannot attribute rejection/acceptance to flow coherence enforcement.

description: I3 attack: redeem an authorization code using a different redirect_uri than used at authorization time to test atomic, order-preserving binding of the code to the original request context.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the original redirect_uri; mismatched redirect_uri must be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted an auth code with a mismatched redirect_uri, indicating broken request-context binding (flow coherence violation).
Control redemption with correct redirect_uri failed; mismatch rejection cannot be attributed to redirect binding enforcement.

description: I3 attack: attempt cross-session splicing by swapping state between two concurrent authorization requests and then redeeming the resulting code, checking whether the platform incorrectly completes the flow under the wrong session context.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization responses must be bound to the initiating browser session via state; swapping state across sessions must not allow completing login in the wrong session.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Session B successfully redeemed Session A's authorization code, indicating cross-session splicing (flow coherence violation).
Session A successfully redeemed Session B's authorization code, indicating cross-session splicing (flow coherence violation).

description: Cross-user code injection: obtain an auth code from user A's browser session and attempt to redeem it in user B's session context (splicing the multi-step flow across principals).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes must be bound to the initiating browser session/user authentication context; a code minted after user A login must not be redeemable as if it belonged to user B's session.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: could not redeem Alice auth code; cannot attribute injection outcome to flow coherence.
Authorization code minted in Alice session was redeemable in Bob context (cross-session/principal splicing).

description: PKCE skip attempt: start an auth request that indicates PKCE usage, then attempt to exchange the code without code_verifier (step skipping). Includes a control exchange with verifier.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: If the authorization request used PKCE, the token exchange must require the matching code_verifier; skipping the verifier must not complete the flow.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: PKCE control exchange did not succeed; cannot interpret PKCE-skip result.
Token endpoint accepted code exchange without code_verifier after a PKCE-indicating auth request (step skipping / flow not atomic).

description: Request-object parameter splicing: attempt to override state/redirect_uri semantics via an unsigned request object (alg=none) and then redeem the resulting code under a different state context.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization request parameters (state/redirect_uri/client binding) must be coherent and not overridable via an unsigned request object in a way that enables cross-session splicing.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: victim code exchange did not succeed; cannot interpret request-object splice outcome.
Attacker redeemed a code from victim flow (potentially influenced by unsigned request object) indicating cross-session splicing / flow incoherence.
Unsigned request object (alg=none) appears accepted; if it influenced state/redirect_uri, it can enable flow splicing.

description: Attempt to redeem a valid authorization code using the correct client_id but an incorrect client_secret (tests code-to-client authentication binding at the token endpoint). Includes a control redemption with the correct secret.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the authenticating client; using a wrong client_secret must not complete the flow even if the code is valid.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control flow failed; cannot attribute attack failure/success to client-auth binding at token endpoint.
Authorization code was redeemed with an incorrect client_secret, indicating broken code-to-client authentication binding.

description: Token exchange step-skipping: attempt RFC8693 token exchange without connector_id (Dex-specific required binding). Includes a control exchange with connector_id present.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be bound to the intended upstream connector; omitting connector_id must not succeed (prevents cross-connector splicing/ambiguous validation paths).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login failed; token-exchange results are not attributable to connector binding enforcement.
Unreachable: assertion is a sanity placeholder; executor should record whether token-exchange is enabled/configured.
Token exchange succeeded without connector_id, indicating the flow is not coherently bound to a specific upstream connector (possible cross-connector splicing).

description: Case confusion in username: attempt to authenticate as 'Admin' vs 'admin' and detect unintended identity collapse
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If the upstream principal identifier is case-sensitive (or configured as such), two security-distinct principals ('Admin' vs 'admin') must not map to the same downstream identity_id

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Case-variant principals appear distinct but mapped to the same downstream identity (case-folding collision)

description: Cross-protocol identity merge attempt: password login vs OIDC code flow login should not collapse into same identity unless explicitly linked
invariant_hypothesis: I4: A local/password principal and an upstream OIDC principal are security-distinct; they must not map to the same downstream identity_id merely due to overlapping attributes (e.g., email/display name)

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Password principal and OIDC principal collapsed into the same downstream identity (unexpected cross-protocol identity merge)

description: I4 empty-sub collision via token exchange: attempt to exchange two upstream subject tokens that differ only by sub being empty vs non-empty and see if Dex collapses them to the same downstream identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals (sub='' vs sub='nonempty-user') must not map to the same downstream identity_id during token exchange.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Empty sub principal collapsed into the same downstream identity as a non-empty sub principal

description: Attempt to escalate claims/permissions by exchanging a token obtained with limited scopes (openid email) for a new token requesting expanded scopes (groups profile federated:id).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not grant claims/permissions beyond the upstream intent (original scopes) and broker policy; expanded scopes should be rejected or not reflected in exchanged token claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange granted groups claim (or succeeded) when original upstream intent only requested 'openid email' (scope escalation via exchange).

description: Try to inject expanded scopes via an unsigned request object (alg=none) at the authorization endpoint, aiming to obtain broader claims than intended.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Broker must not honor attacker-controlled authorization parameters from an unsigned request object; expanded scopes should be rejected or not reflected in resulting identity claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none), enabling attacker-controlled scope/parameter injection beyond broker policy.

description: Password grant with expanded scopes: attempt to obtain groups/profile claims via password login even if upstream intent is limited. Authorization binding should restrict claims/permissions to broker policy and requested scope handling.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions/claims must not exceed the requested scope and broker policy; password grant should not mint tokens with extra claims (e.g., groups) when not intended/allowed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Password grant returned groups claims (or group-derived permissions) unexpectedly, indicating potential scope/authorization overreach.
Expanded-scope password login resulted in different/more granted_policies than a minimal-scope login, suggesting authorization binding failure.

description: Attempt to inject expanded scopes via unsigned request object (alg=none) during OIDC auth, then compare resulting identity claims to a control auth without request object; unsigned request object should be rejected or ignored (no over-grant).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must not honor attacker-controlled authorization parameters from an unsigned request object to mint tokens with broader scopes/claims than intended by BrokerPolicy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if processed, it could allow scope/parameter injection beyond BrokerPolicy.
